newsitem.title: USA: White House counsel denies indictment expectation.
newsitem.headline: White House counsel denies indictment expectation.

text.p: The head of President Bill Clinton's Whitewater damage control team said on Wednesday she had been misquoted in a newspaper report predicting that some current or former White House aides would be indicted in the affair by the end of February.

Jane Sherburne, the White House special counsel who coordinates Whitewater matters, said she had no idea whether Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth Starr would seek further indictments, contrary to remarks attributed to her in the Wednesday edition of USA Today.

"I have no expectation. I don't know what Ken Starr is planning, period," she said in a telephone interview with Reuters. Referring to what she called the erroneous USA Today reporter's account, she added: "I don't know what he strung together there."

The newspaper cited Sherburne as saying the White House "had expected indictments at the end of the year." She was reported as adding that was set back until at least February after James McDougal, a former Clinton business partner convicted on fraud charges in May, started cooperating with Starr.
The reporter in question, Tom Squitieri, said he stood by his account. "She made those remarks to me in a telephone interview on Monday," he said.
In general, Whitewater relates to the Clintons' business dealings in the 1980s as the first family of Arkansas and their White House response to investigators' subsequent scrutiny.
